name: Big-O Notation
description: Big-O notation describes how an algorithm's runtime or memory usage grows as the input size N increases, focusing on the dominant term and ignoring constant factors. It lets us compare algorithms independently of hardware and input specifics.
examples: O(1) — constant: hash table lookup, array index access.
O(N) — linear: single pass over an array.
O(N log N) — linearithmic: merge sort, heap sort.
comparison: O(1) < O(log N) < O(N) < O(N log N) < O(N^2) < O(2^N) < O(N!)
tips: Drop constants and lower-order terms: 3N + 20 is O(N).
Different loops add, nested loops multiply.
Two-pointer / sliding window often reduce O(N^2) to O(N).
common_mistakes: Counting N as both input size and something else.
Treating the best case as the worst case when asked for Big-O.
